title: Huangdi Neijing (Yellow Emperor's Inner Canon)
summary: A Chinese medical classic framed as a dialogue between the semi-legendary Huangdi and his physician about health, disease and treatment. Though credited to Huangdi, it is thought to be a compilation of texts by several authors, dated from about 300 BCE to the first century BCE, and has been called the first collection of mature classical medical writings.

uncertainty.note: Sources differ: an NIH-hosted article suggests a later origin around 300 BC; Encyclopedia.com dates it c. first century BCE. Range spans both. The traditional attribution to Huangdi (c. 2600 BC) is described by the source as semi-mythical.

where.modern_name: China (country-level proxy; the sources give no place of composition)
where.historical_name: China, Warring States to Han period (place of compilation not stated in sources)

importance.justification: Foundational text of Chinese classical medicine, called in the sources the first collection of mature classical writings on the subject.
